explanation: The environment setup is complete and the full analysis runs, but the reviewed endpoint set cannot be satisfied by the frozen export code. Test 1 (un-adapted original) failed offline on DNS resolution for the two remote read_table URLs, as expected. After the documented input-path adaptation, test 2 ran the complete analysis offline from a fresh venv and working directory: exit 0 in 30.18 s (limit 600 s), peak child RSS ~0.98 GiB (limit 8 GiB), staged inputs verified byte-identical (/inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz, /inputs/hg38.ensGene.gtf.gz, files: 2, staged_inputs_verified: true). All five peak-to-gene assignment tables were computed and serialized: 696,473 CSV lines each (696,472 chromosome-filtered CDS gene rows + header, matching the shell-observed filtered genes table of 696,472 rows x 9 cols) and 176.8-179.7 MB per file, well within disk limits. Four declared artifacts were produced (peaks_closest.csv sha256 271f932c..., peaks_closest_upstream_nodir.csv b783..., wait: 271f932c.../b783501d... per receipt, peaks_closest_upstream_dir.csv 2896bd55..., peaks_closest_downstream_dir.csv f9b7c427...). BLOCKER: the frozen, must-not-modify exports.py serializes peaks_closest_downstream_nodir to the filename 'peaks_closest_downstream_dir_placeholder.csv' (line 17-19 of the appended export, visible in the test-1 failure log and plan.json export_code) instead of the inventory name 'peaks_closest_downstream_nodir.csv'. Consequently that declared artifact is never written and an undeclared placeholder file appears; the controller reports declared_artifacts_present=false and reference_failed. This is an internal inconsistency between the reviewed export code and the reviewed artifact inventory (a filename typo), not an environment, dependency, or data failure: dependencies installed cleanly, both data sources are reachable and stable, and the scientific computation itself completed. No setup-side change can resolve it because the controller appends the frozen export code after analysis.py. Correcting the export filename (or the inventory entry) to peaks_closest_downstream_nodir.csv and re-running should pass, since everything else is demonstrated to work. A separate pre-existing flag, the sha_declaration_error on peaks_closest_downstream_dir.csv (plan hash b783501d... vs actual f9b7c427...), reflects that the preparation stage recorded hash placeholders without ever executing; the actual bytes are deterministic from the re-run, so re-recording after a corrected export would resolve it.
source_adaptations: Offline input-path adaptation in analysis.py: the ENCODE narrowPeak URL 'https://www.encodeproject.org/files/ENCFF401MQL/@@download/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz' passed to bioframe.read_table(schema='narrowPeak') was replaced with '/inputs/ENCFF401MQL.bed.gz', staged byte-identically from the same URL by stage-inputs.sh (verified by the controller in both tests: sha256 c0bf...; identical across three independent downloads I made). The reference execution has no network, so the remote read was impossible. No other change to this cell.

Offline input-path adaptation in analysis.py: the genes_url constant 'https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenpath/hg38/bigZips/genes/hg38.ensGene.gtf.gz' was replaced with '/inputs/hg38.ensGene.gtf.gz', staged byte-identically from the same URL by stage-inputs.sh (sha256 7a16...; identical across three independent downloads). The read_table(..., schema='gtf') call, the .query('feature=="CDS"') filter, and all downstream filtering/assignment/plotting code are unchanged. Both adaptations only relocate the exact original bytes; they do not alter which bytes the analysis reads.
unresolved_assumptions: Both source endpoints serve live, non-versioned files (ENCODE ENCFF401MQL and UCSC hg38.ensGene.gtf.gz): neither site publishes an immutable checksum, so the recorded hashes are observational; the staged bytes were identical across three independent fetches during setup, but an upstream change would change the outputs.

bioframe==0.8.0 was pinned as the version of the referenced source revision (read from the repo's pyproject.toml at 95007ed); on the image's Python 3.13 it resolves to pandas 3.0.6 / numpy 2.5.4, a newer stack than the tutorial's era, so exact output values could in principle differ from an older pandas/numpy resolution even though all bioframe.closest calls, the nullable Int64 distance handling and the plot calls succeeded.

The export filename mismatch (peaks_closest_downstream_nodir.csv declared vs 'peaks_closest_downstream_dir_placeholder.csv' written by the frozen export code) is assumed to be an error in the reviewed export that will be corrected there; I did not work around it in analysis.py or staging because the reviewed exports and endpoint inventory must not be changed at this stage.

The plan.json recorded sha256 placeholders for artifacts (e.g. peaks_closest_downstream_dir.csv) were never executed/back-filled; after the export filename is corrected, hashes must be re-recorded from a real run rather than trusted from the preparation stage.
